(p-197) Surah al-'Asr

It is Makkan, and its verses are three.

﴿By the time (al-'Asr)﴾ He, Glorified is He, swears by the 'Asr prayer (the afternoon prayer) because of its dazzling merit; or by the late afternoon (al-'ashiyy), which is the time between the sun's passing its zenith and its setting, just as He swore by the forenoon (al-duha); or by the era of prophethood, because its merit over all other eras is manifest; or by time (al-dahr), because it encompasses the wonders of affairs, both those that endure and those that pass away.

﴿Indeed, mankind is in loss﴾ that is: a loss in their trades and their endeavors, and in spending their lives on their own pursuits. The definite article (in "al-insān") denotes the genus, and the indefinite form (in "khusr") conveys magnification.

﴿Except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾ for they are engaged in a trade that will never perish, since they have sold the fleeting and base and bought the lasting and precious, and have exchanged the enduring righteous deeds for what goes away in the morning and returns in the evening. What a bargain it is, and how profitable! This is an explanation of how they perfect themselves. And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿and enjoin one another to the truth﴾ and so on, is an explanation of how they perfect others. That is: they charge one another with the matter that is firmly established, which there is no way to deny, and whose fair effects never cease in the two abodes. It is all that is good: faith in Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and following His Books and His Messengers in every belief and every action. ﴿and enjoin one another to patience﴾ that is: patience in refraining from the acts of disobedience for which the soul longs by virtue of human nature, and in performing the acts of obedience which are hard for it to carry out, or patience in what Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, tests His servants with. The singling out of this mutual enjoining by mention, although it is included under mutual enjoining to the truth, is to bring out the perfect care due to it; or because the first refers to the rank of worship ('ibadah), which is doing what pleases Allah, the Exalted, while the second refers to the rank of servitude ('ubudiyyah), which is being content with what Allah, the Exalted, has done. For what is meant by patience (sabr) is not merely restraining the soul from what it yearns for in doing and leaving, but rather receiving what comes from Him, the Exalted, with graciousness and contentment with it, outwardly and inwardly.

From the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Whoever recites Surat al-'Asr, Allah, the Exalted, will forgive him, and he will be among those who enjoined one another to the truth and enjoined one another to patience."
